proof_summary: Take the counterexample \(n=2^{14}\cdot4409\cdot458009=33085221781504\), where \(4409\) and \(458009\) are prime. Multiplicativity gives \(\sigma(n)=66183576284700\) and \((\mathbf 1*\sigma)(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}\sigma(d)=132367152569399\), so \(a(n)=2\sigma(n)-(\mathbf 1*\sigma)(n)=1\), although \(n\) is neither exceptional value.
